html:
The Iningai are an Aboriginal Australian people of central west Queensland, in the country around today's Longreach. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their land is wide grassland on the Thomson River and its creeks, part of the inland that drains toward Lake Eyre. Little is recorded of their life before colonisation. Sheep stations spread here in the 1860s and 1870s, and Longreach became a wool town. The airline Qantas had its early base there in the 1920s. Neighbours on the map include the Kuungkari, the Yagalingu and the Miyan. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
